questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: AC voltage applied to a resistor
questions.question: If an alternating voltage V(t) = V₀ sin(ωt) is applied to a pure resistor, the average power dissipated is P_AC. If a steady direct current (DC) voltage of magnitude V₀ is applied to the same resistor, the power dissipated is P_DC. What is the exact ratio of P_AC : P_DC?
questions.explanation: For an AC voltage V(t) = V₀ sin(ωt), average power P_AC = (V_rms)² / R. Since V_rms = V₀ / √2, P_AC = (V₀ / √2)² / R = V₀² / (2R). For a DC voltage V₀, power P_DC = V₀² / R. The ratio P_AC : P_DC = (V₀² / 2R) : (V₀² / R) = 1/2 : 1 = 1 : 2.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Representation of AC current and voltage by rotating vectors – phasors
questions.question: In the phasor representation of alternating currents and voltages, the physical length of the rotating vector (phasor) corresponds exactly to which property of the AC quantity?
options: The average value over a half cycle
questions.explanation: In a phasor diagram, an alternating quantity is represented by a rotating vector. The length (magnitude) of this vector strictly corresponds to the peak amplitude (V₀ or I₀) of the alternating quantity, while its projection on the vertical or horizontal axis represents the instantaneous value.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Power in AC circuit: the power factor
questions.question: A purely inductive AC circuit is connected to an alternating voltage source of frequency f. What is the frequency at which the instantaneous power supplied to the inductor oscillates?
questions.explanation: Instantaneous power P(t) = V(t) · I(t). For a pure inductor, V(t) = V_m sin(ωt) and I(t) = -I_m cos(ωt). P(t) = -V_m I_m sin(ωt) cos(ωt) = -(V_m I_m / 2) sin(2ωt). The power function is a sine wave with an angular frequency of 2ω. Therefore, its standard frequency is exactly 2f.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Transformers
questions.question: A student accidentally connects the primary coil of a step-up transformer (having a turns ratio of 1 : 10) to a steady 12 V DC car battery. What will be the steady voltage measured across the secondary coil?
questions.explanation: Transformers operate exclusively on the principle of electromagnetic induction, which strictly requires a changing magnetic flux (AC). A steady DC battery provides a constant current, creating a static, non-changing magnetic field. With dΦ/dt = 0, Faraday's law dictates that the induced EMF in the secondary coil is precisely 0 V.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: AC voltage applied to a series LCR circuit
questions.question: Dimensional analysis reveals that the quantity √(L/C) (where L is inductance and C is capacitance) shares its dimensional formula with which of the following physical quantities?
questions.explanation: The impedance of an inductor is X_L = ωL, so L has dimensions of Resistance · Time. The impedance of a capacitor is X_C = 1/(ωC), so C has dimensions of Time / Resistance. The ratio L/C has dimensions (Resistance · Time) / (Time / Resistance) = Resistance². Therefore, √(L/C) has the precise dimension of Electrical Resistance (Ω).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: AC voltage applied to a capacitor
questions.question: A sinusoidal waveform graph shows Voltage (V) and Current (I) plotted against time. The current wave I reaches its positive peak exactly when the voltage wave V crosses zero with a positive slope (i.e., the current is a quarter of a cycle ahead of the voltage). What kind of ideal circuit component is this AC source connected to?
options: A series combination of an inductor and resistor
questions.explanation: The scenario describes a situation where Current (I) reaches its maximum positive value a quarter cycle (90° or π/2) before Voltage (V) reaches its maximum positive value. In standard AC theory, the phrase 'Current leads Voltage by 90°' is the defining mathematical relationship for a purely capacitive circuit.
questions.imagePrompt: A sinusoidal waveform graph showing Voltage (V) and Current (I) plotted against time. The current wave I reaches its positive peak exactly when the voltage wave V crosses zero with a positive slope (i.e., I leads V by a quarter cycle).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: AC voltage applied to an inductor
questions.question: An air-core inductor is connected in series with a glowing incandescent bulb across an AC voltage source. If a soft iron core is slowly inserted completely into the inductor, what will happen to the brightness of the bulb?
options: It will instantly drop to zero.
questions.explanation: An inductor's reactance is X_L = ωL. The inductance L depends on the permeability of the core (μ). A soft iron core has a high relative permeability (μ_r ≫ 1), which drastically increases L. Increased L means increased total impedance Z. Since I_rms = V_rms / Z, the current drops. Consequently, the power dissipated by the bulb (I_rms² R) strictly decreases, causing it to dim.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: AC voltage applied to a series LCR circuit
questions.question: In a series LCR circuit connected to an AC source, the voltage drops across the resistor, inductor, and capacitor are measured using AC voltmeters. The readings are V_R = 40 V, V_L = 60 V, and V_C = 30 V respectively. What is the net RMS voltage of the AC source?
questions.explanation: In a series LCR circuit, AC voltages must be added via phasor vector addition, not simple algebraic addition. V_net = √[V_R² + (V_L - V_C)²]. V_net = √[40² + (60 - 30)²] = √[40² + 30²] = √[1600 + 900] = √2500 = 50 V.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Transformers
questions.question: A non-ideal transformer has an efficiency of 90%. It is connected to a 200 V AC mains supply. The secondary coil delivers a current of 8 A to a load at a voltage of 100 V. What is the current drawn from the primary mains supply?
questions.explanation: Output power P_out = V_s · I_s = 100 × 8 = 800 W. Efficiency η = P_out / P_in ⟹ 0.90 = 800 / P_in ⟹ P_in = 800 / 0.9 = 8000/9 W. Input power P_in = V_p · I_p ⟹ I_p = P_in / V_p = (8000/9) / 200 = 40/9 ≈ 4.44 A.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Transformers
questions.question: Two closely coupled coils have a mutual inductance of 0.005 H. The alternating current in the primary coil varies according to the equation I = 10 sin(100π t) Amperes. What is the absolute maximum (peak) induced EMF in the secondary coil?
questions.explanation: The induced EMF in the secondary is given by Faraday's law of mutual induction: E₂ = -M (dI₁/dt). Given I₁(t) = 10 sin(100π t). dI₁/dt = 10 × 100π cos(100π t) = 1000π cos(100π t). |E₂| = 0.005 × 1000π cos(100π t) = 5π cos(100π t). The peak (maximum) amplitude of this induced EMF is simply the coefficient, 5π V.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: AC voltage applied to a series LCR circuit
questions.question: A plot shows the Impedance (Z) on the y-axis versus the angular frequency (ω) on the x-axis for a specific AC circuit. The curve is U-shaped, starting very high at low frequencies, smoothly dipping to a minimum value exactly equal to the resistance R at a specific frequency ω₀, and then rising linearly at high frequencies. Which of the following statements about the circuit at ω = ω₀ is FALSE?
options: The power factor of the circuit is unity (1).
The current and voltage are exactly in phase.
The voltages across the inductor and capacitor are zero.
questions.explanation: The graph represents an LCR series circuit passing through electrical resonance. At ω₀, Z = R, which is the minimum impedance. At resonance, X_L = X_C, so the reactive components completely cancel each other out (V_L - V_C = 0). However, the *individual* voltages V_L and V_C are NOT zero. Due to the high Q-factor, V_L and V_C can be significantly higher than the source voltage. Thus, statement (C) is FALSE.
questions.imagePrompt: A plot showing Impedance Z on the y-axis versus angular frequency ω on the x-axis for an AC circuit. The curve is U-shaped, starting high, dipping to a minimum value denoted as R at a specific frequency ω₀, and then rising again.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: AC voltage applied to a series LCR circuit
questions.question:
PASSAGE: A series LCR circuit is constructed with a resistance R = 15 Ω, an inductance L = 0.44 H, and a capacitance C = 10 μF. It is connected to an AC voltage source described by V(t) = 100 sin(500 t) Volts, where time t is in seconds.

What is the peak amplitude of the current (I₀) flowing through this circuit?
questions.explanation: From the passage: V_m = 100 V, ω = 500 rad/s. Inductive Reactance X_L = ωL = 500 × 0.44 = 220 Ω. Capacitive Reactance X_C = 1/(ωC) = 1/(500 × 10 × 10⁻⁶) = 1/(5 × 10⁻³) = 1000/5 = 200 Ω. Impedance Z = √[R² + (X_L - X_C)²] = √[15² + (220 - 200)²] = √[225 + 400] = √625 = 25 Ω. Peak current I₀ = V_m / Z = 100 / 25 = 4 A.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Power in AC circuit: the power factor
questions.question: PASSAGE CONTINUED: What is the average electrical power dissipated by the circuit over one complete cycle?
questions.explanation: Average power P = I_rms² R = (I₀ / √2)² R = (I₀² / 2) R. Using values from previous question: I₀ = 4 A, R = 15 Ω. P = (16 / 2) × 15 = 8 × 15 = 120 W.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Representation of AC current and voltage by rotating vectors – phasors
questions.question: PASSAGE CONTINUED: What is the phase difference between the source voltage and the circuit current, and which quantity leads?
questions.explanation: Phase angle φ is given by tan(φ) = (X_L - X_C) / R = (220 - 200) / 15 = 20 / 15 = 4/3. Since X_L > X_C, the circuit is predominantly inductive. In an inductive circuit, the Voltage leads the Current. Thus, Voltage leads current by tan⁻¹(4/3).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Alternating Current
questions.question: A highly irregular alternating current flowing through a wire is mathematically modeled by the equation i(t) = 3 + 4sin(ωt) Amperes. What will a standard AC ammeter (which strictly measures the RMS value) read when connected in series with this wire?
questions.explanation: The current contains a DC component (I_dc = 3 A) and an AC component (I_ac = 4sin(ωt)). The general RMS formula is I_rms = √[(1/T) ∫ i(t)² dt]. Expanding: i(t)² = (3 + 4sin(ωt))² = 9 + 24sin(ωt) + 16sin²(ωt). Taking the average over one cycle: ⟨9⟩ = 9. ⟨24sin(ωt)⟩ = 0. ⟨16sin²(ωt)⟩ = 16 × (1/2) = 8. I_rms = √(9 + 0 + 8) = √17 A.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Power in AC circuit: the power factor
questions.question: A certain electrical coil draws a steady current of 4 A when connected to a 100 V DC source. When the exact same coil is connected to a 100 V, 50 Hz AC source, it only draws 2.4 A. What is the power factor of the coil in the AC circuit?
questions.explanation: DC circuit isolates resistance: R = V_dc / I_dc = 100 / 4 = 25 Ω. AC circuit gives total impedance: Z = V_ac / I_ac = 100 / 2.4 = 1000 / 24 = 125/3 Ω. Power factor cos(φ) = R / Z = 25 / (125/3) = 75 / 125 = 3/5 = 0.6.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: AC voltage applied to a series LCR circuit
questions.question: A schematic AC circuit displays a resistor R connected in series with a parallel tank combination. The tank consists of an ideal inductor L and an ideal capacitor C in parallel with each other. An AC voltage source V(t) is connected across the entire global arrangement. At what specific angular frequency ω will the total current drawn from the AC source be mathematically minimized (approaching zero for ideal components)?
options: The current can never be minimized to zero in this configuration.
questions.explanation: The image describes an anti-resonance circuit (Parallel LC tank). The admittance of the parallel LC tank is Y_tank = 1/(jωL) + jωC = (1 - ω²LC) / (jωL). The impedance of the tank is Z_tank = 1 / Y_tank = (jωL) / (1 - ω²LC). When ω = 1/√(LC), the denominator becomes exactly zero, making Z_tank → ∞. With infinite impedance in series with R, the total current drawn from the source drops to its absolute mathematical minimum (zero for ideal components).
questions.imagePrompt: An electrical circuit schematic showing an AC voltage source connected to a resistor R in series. This is then followed by a parallel combination of an ideal inductor L and an ideal capacitor C.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: AC voltage applied to a series LCR circuit
questions.question: A series LCR circuit used as a bandpass filter has R = 10 Ω, L = 0.1 H, and C = 10 μF. What are the approximate values of the two half-power frequencies (lower and upper cutoff frequencies) in rad/s for this circuit?
questions.explanation: Resonant frequency ω₀ = 1/√(LC) = 1/√(0.1 × 10 × 10⁻⁶) = 1/√(10⁻⁶) = 1000 rad/s. The bandwidth is Δω = R/L = 10 / 0.1 = 100 rad/s. For a high-Q circuit, the resonance curve is symmetric, so the half-power frequencies are given by ω = ω₀ ± (Δω/2). ω = 1000 ± 50. This gives 950 rad/s and 1050 rad/s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: AC voltage applied to a series LCR circuit
questions.question: An incandescent lamp is rated to operate optimally at 100 V and 100 W. It is required to run this lamp safely on a 200 V, 50 Hz AC mains supply. To avoid wasting energy as heat in a series resistor, a pure capacitor is connected in series with the lamp instead. What is the required capacitance? (Take π = 3.14 and √3 = 1.732)
questions.explanation: Lamp resistance R = V_rated² / P_rated = 100² / 100 = 100 Ω. Safe current I = P_rated / V_rated = 100 / 100 = 1 A. When run on 200 V mains, the required total impedance Z to limit current to 1 A is Z = 200 / 1 = 200 Ω. In a series RC circuit, Z = √(R² + X_C²) ⟹ 200² = 100² + X_C² ⟹ X_C = √(40000 - 10000) = √(30000) = 100√3 ≈ 173.2 Ω. X_C = 1 / (2πfC) ⟹ 173.2 = 1 / (2 × 3.14 × 50 × C) ⟹ C = 1 / (314 × 173.2) = 1 / 54384 ≈ 1.838 × 10⁻⁵ F = 18.4 μF.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Power in AC circuit: the power factor
questions.question: A large industrial AC electric motor can be modeled as a resistor of 30 Ω in series with an inductive reactance of 40 Ω. It operates on a 250 V, 50 Hz AC power line. To avoid fines from the power company, the factory must install a capacitor in parallel with the motor to achieve a perfect power factor of unity (1.0) for the combined circuit. What must be the exact capacitance of this parallel capacitor?
questions.explanation: The motor's admittance Y_m = 1/Z_m = 1 / (R + jX_L) = 1 / (30 + j40). Multiply by conjugate: Y_m = (30 - j40) / (30² + 40²) = (30 - j40) / 2500 = 0.012 - j0.016 S. To achieve unity power factor, the reactive (imaginary) part of the total circuit admittance must be completely cancelled out. A capacitor added in parallel provides an admittance Y_c = +jωC. Total Admittance Y_tot = (0.012 - j0.016) + jωC. For unity power factor, the imaginary term must be zero: ωC = 0.016. Given f = 50 Hz, ω = 100π. 100πC = 0.016 ⟹ C = 0.016 / 100π = (160 × 10⁻⁶) / π F = 160/π μF.
